patterns.name: The Shutdown Spiral
patterns.description: A bad-news event at work triggers an immediate withdrawal: blinds closed, phone off, food skipped, plans cancelled, isolation sought almost as self-punishment for having cared — followed eventually by a climb back out.
patterns.trigger: Negative or destabilizing feedback/news from Marcus or work (criticism, whiplash feedback, restructuring updates)

instances.note: Marcus tears apart dashboard in review; Jordan lies about a headache, goes dark, two hours staring at the wall, no dinner.
Whiplash 'too safe' critique; Jordan cancels on Mika, skips food, ignores Pepper, sits on the floor in the dark.
Flat corporate restructuring news; Jordan goes home at 4pm, cancels on Dev with a cover story, blinds shut.
Reorg lands (legacy marketing); shutdown occurs but only lasts twenty minutes before Jordan gets up and goes to Groundwork.

patterns.name: Groundwork Resurrection
patterns.description: What actually pulls Jordan out of a shutdown isn't rest or waiting it out — it's physically leaving the apartment and going to Groundwork to build something on Coda, after which competence and feeling human again reliably return.
patterns.trigger: Being forced or forcing oneself out of the apartment after a shutdown period

instances.note: Calls in sick to avoid Marcus, forces trip to Groundwork instead of couch, three hours on metronome feature, competence returns.
Forces through workday, lands at Groundwork, two hours on quick-start cards, comes home to real food and Pepper's head-bonks.
Twenty minutes on the dark couch, then Groundwork for two hours on Coda — shortest shutdown yet, done alone.
At Groundwork, cracks the free-play design problem, ninety-minute prototype breakthrough, reframes job as one thread among several.

patterns.name: Someone Has to Pull the Gears Loose
patterns.description: Jordan doesn't self-rescue from withdrawal alone (at least early on) — someone from outside physically shows up or intervenes, most often Mika, to end the isolation.
patterns.trigger: Jordan going dark/isolating after bad work news

instances.note: Mikayla's low-key coffee-shop check-in, no advice, just company, reinforces the pattern of needing outside contact.
Jordan apologizes to Mika, who says she knew Jordan would bounce back.
Mika shows up uninvited with pad thai to pull Jordan out of the shutdown.
Mika drives Jordan to the open mic after they nearly back out three times, forcing follow-through.

patterns.name: Blackout First, Disclosure Late
patterns.description: Jordan withholds hard truths from the people closest to them to 'protect' them or avoid vulnerability, then eventually discloses late — after which things get lighter, not worse.
patterns.trigger: Fear of worrying someone or being seen as not fine

instances.note: Tells Mom things are 'fine and good,' withholding work stress and reorg news.
Cancels on Dev with a fake excuse rather than admitting the real reason.
Goes back and tells Dev the truth about the cancellation; Dev responds with their own admission.
Finally tells Mom everything about work, five weeks late; her response is sadness, not anger, and sharper questions than Jordan asked himself.

patterns.name: Coda as Counterweight
patterns.description: Jordan's most productive creative stretches on Coda arrive specifically as a response to work instability or emotional low points — the app functions as both refuge and, eventually, recognized achievement, though this takes months for Jordan to believe.
patterns.trigger: Work stress or emotional destabilization needing an outlet

instances.note: Groundwork environment enables real progress on streak counter/flames, contrasted with couch-and-feeds spiral at home.
Mika names explicitly that Jordan retreats from Coda when work is unstable and returns to it to feel better.
Breakthrough free-play prototype built in ninety minutes at Groundwork after Monday's low.
Writing the Coda case study honestly becomes the strongest portfolio piece, finally confirming what Mika and Lena predicted months earlier.

patterns.name: Needs a Push
patterns.description: Jordan reliably needs outside pressure — a friend's insistence, a deadline, someone else deciding — to follow through on things Jordan actually wants but wouldn't initiate alone.
patterns.trigger: An opportunity or value Jordan cares about but is anxious or avoidant about acting on unprompted

instances.note: Mika talks Jordan out of cancelling the first walk with Dev.
Mika signs Jordan up for the open mic without asking; practicing becomes a small joy Jordan 'always forgets' they like.
Mika literally drives Jordan to the open mic after three near-bailouts; the performance becomes a highlight.

patterns.name: The Reflexive Self-Diminishment
patterns.description: When given genuine credit, opportunity, or validation, Jordan's automatic first response is self-doubt that contradicts what they actually know to be true about their own competence — a reflex that has to be caught and corrected by someone else or by Jordan themself after the fact.
patterns.trigger: Being offered validation, opportunity, or recognition tied to real skill

instances.note: Reflexively tells Lena 'I don't think I'd have good enough experience' for the Northlight referral, contradicting known validated work.
Distrusts the good news from the phone screen with Ana, needing to see things written down to believe them, even as the call goes well.

patterns.name: Running It Out
patterns.description: Solo or accompanied runs at Greenwood Park function as the place where real decisions get made and residue gets processed, distinct from the Groundwork/Coda recovery track.
patterns.trigger: An unresolved decision or emotional residue (anxiety, a bad dream, adrenaline) needing to be worked through

instances.note: Early solitary run after 4am anxiety-dream wake-up, used to cope with restructuring dread.
Solo run with hill-trail extension becomes the setting where the lease-renewal decision actually gets made.
Run after the Ana phone screen to burn off adrenaline; reframe of reorg as 'inconvenience' caught in real time on the hill trail.

patterns.name: The Empty Office Dream
patterns.description: A recurring anxiety dream (empty office, phantom typing, no exit) tracks Jordan's suppressed restructuring dread, and its evolution across instances mirrors real-world progress on the underlying fear.
patterns.trigger: Suppressed anxiety about the restructuring/job instability surfacing at night

instances.note: First occurrence: emptied office, phantom typing, vanished elevator, no exit; 4am wake-up.
Third occurrence (dreamed night of 9/11): same setting, but this time Jordan finds the stairs and walks out.
